newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-BORGES RETAINS MEN'S 200 FREESTYLE WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-BORGES RETAINS MEN'S 200 FREESTYLE WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Brazil's Gustavo Borges retained his 200 metres freestyle title, dominating the final at the world short-course swimming championships on Thursday.

Borges led throughout the race in his fluid loping style, taking early charge and never relinquishing his hold on the title he won in 1995 on home territory in Rio de Janeiro. The rest scrapped for the other medals.
Borges, who took the Olympic silver at the 1992 Barcelona Games and the bronze at the 1996 Atlanta Games, won comfortably in one minute 45.45 seconds.
New Zealand's Trent Bray claimed the silver in 1:45.81 and German Lars Conrad the bronze in 1:46.44 to add to the European short-course gold he won in Rostock last December.
Australia's Michael Klim, who had earlier taken the bronze in the 100 metres butterfly, just missed another medal. He was fourth in 1:46.72.
